text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The International Monetary Fund has asked Pakistan not to extend sales tax collection at the retail level as the country lacked the machinery to make such a venture possible.
- The government plans to reduce the mark-up (interest) rate of commercial banks in 1997/98 (July-June) to revive the competitiveness of local industry.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has announced a five percent cut in the statutory liquidity ratio of non-bank financial institutions.
- Pakistan has fixed the overall borrowing limit at 148 billion rupees ($3.655 billion) in the 1997/98 budget to keep the deficit at five percent of gross domestic product.
- Pakistani officials held talks on the Afghan issue with the visiting Turkmenistan foreign minister and Russian deputy foreign minister.
- Prisoners in Hyderabad jail rioted against keeping several inmates in solitary confinement for the past month.
- The Sindh provincial government will allot 100 acres of land to foreign investors in the industrial estate in north Karachi.
- A 135.6-megawatt power project being executed by the Japan Power Generation Ltd on the outskirts of Lahore is in the doldrums due to a cost escalation of 280 million rupees.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said banks will recover 33 percent of the 127 billion rupees in bad loans over the next three months under the new foreclosure laws.
- The Ehtesab (accountability) cell will start sending 34 cases of alleged corruption to the Ehtesab Commissioner next week.
